newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Rubber prices stay strong at Colombo auction.
newsitem.headline: Rubber prices stay strong at Colombo auction.

text.p: Sri Lankan rubber prices remained strong at Thursday's auction as buyers covered positions before wintering sets in and reduces latex output, brokers and buyers said.
Brokers said prices were unaffected by news of the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping as China was not a major buyer of Sri Lanka rubber.

Best latex one-x, the purest grade, increased marginally to 74.65 rupees per kg from 74.50 on Tuesday when the auction was last held. Number one fetched 74 rupees as compared to 73.80 on Tuesday. RSS 1 improved to 62.20 from 62 rupees.
A total of 192 tonnes of latex crepe and 65 tonnes of scrap were on offer.
"Wintering effects are setting in. We're going in to a period where latex will be drying up fast," said a leading exporter. "So we're seing a lot of short-covering."
Wintering is when the tree goes into a period of annual hibernation during the dry months of the first quarter.
"The market moved up last week and held on to those levels this week," a broker at John Keells said.
